items.title: Barney Bigard Interview, 1969-07-25
items.q: The records that we played were the classic trio, piano, clarinet, and drums. Morton, of course, had used that form earlier on records with Johnny Dodds, with the Jelly Roll Morton trio

ctx.x: Hi Bill, this is Floyd Levin in Los Angeles. This is the 25th of July 1969 and shortly I expect Barney Begard over, at which time I will supply the questions and hopefully he'll come up with some of the answers to help you on your quest for information about Jelly Roll Morton. Okay, we've just played the Victor Trio session, Barney. I assume that you have some memories about that session. Yeah, I was really surprised. I thought I played more than I do now. That's going back, what, 40 years? Yes, it is. Could you…

items.title: 68113_Barney Bigard oral history interview
items.q: the guy that played in his band was Johnny Dodds... he borrowed the E-flat from him so I could learn

ctx.x: You see, he taught me how to read the music and the division of the bars and all that. I had a book, you see. And he taught me that. Then when he found out that I could do pretty well like that, they didn't give me a clarinet at all to start with, which I am very happy until this day, you know, because that would have been double -- you know, like, too much for my little brain to manipulate, trying to read the music, and the fingering of the clarinet. And then my hands were so small, and so they used an E-flat,…

And so the guy that played in his band was Johnny Dodds. He played clarinet in his band, and he had one, so my uncle borrowed his E-flat. Yeah, so he borrowed -- he loaned my uncle his little E-flat clarinet since he wasn't playing in many parades. And only I'd give it back to him when he had a parade to play.
